source_title: BioWare Co-Founder Weighs In On Studio's Closure
source_excerpt:
BioWare co-founder Greg Zeschuk shared his thoughts about the recently confirmed closure of BioWare, lamenting the unfortunate fate of the beloved Mass Effect studio. EA officially confirmed in October that it is closing BioWare , just over 30 years after the studio was founded.
Since the studio's foundation in 1995, BioWare has grown into a staple of the gaming world, with plenty of critically acclaimed games in its library. The company has worked on a number of beloved adaptations of popular properties, including early games in the Baldur's Gate franchise, Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic , and Neverwinter Nights . The studio saw plenty of success with its own franchises as well, creating series like Dragon Age and Mass Effect . Now, EA is officially shutting down BioWare and one of the studio's co-founders is sharing his thoughts.
BioWare Co-Founder Greg Zeschuk Speaks About Studio Closure
In an interview with 80LV , Greg Zeschuk spoke about EA's decision to permanently close the studio. While Zeschuk was saddened by the closure, the former executive shared that he had already made his peace and "gone through all the emotions" after leaving the studio in 2012. Zeschuk lamented the situation for the city of Edmonton, where BioWare's studios were located, saying that the company served as a "beacon of hope and excitement" in a place that is not typically known for game development. He ultimately said that he wasn't surprised by the decision to shut down BioWare, particularly following the acquisition of EA by the Saudi Arabia Public Investment Fund .

Zeschuk laid much of the blame for BioWare's closure on the new owners of EA. The former executive stated that he felt the Saudi PIF's purchase of EA was the "final nail in the coffin" for the studio, saying that BioWare's games "take a long time to make" and it is likely a better business model to "pump out sports games every year." Zeschuk was critical of EA's new Saudi executives not having game development experience, saying that none of them "have ever made a game" and that the PIF does not understand the process of creating games.

The closure of BioWare has already seen plenty of news surface about the studio's previous in-development projects. Leaks have revealed an internal trailer for the fifth game in the Mass Effect series, titled Mass Effect Universe , which teased a new protagonist. The Mass Effect leaks have even seen fans start a campaign to save the franchise following BioWare's closure, with more than 100,000 people already signing the #SaveMassEffect petition . BioWare Technical Director Romain Toutain also revealed that the game was intended to take decisions made in previous Mass Effect games into account, changing the in-game universe.
The purchase of EA has sent a ripple effect through plenty of the company's subsidiaries, not just BioWare. News about multiple EA cancellations have surfaced in recent months, including an in-development spin-off of The Sims internally referred to as Project Lotus . The company also revealed that a popular sports series will be making its long-awaited return in the near future, confirming that EA Sports is reviving the Fight Night franchise , more than 15 years after the last game in the series. EA will likely continue to see more big changes in the future as the studio adjusts to its new ownership.
